newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel steady on sustained buying.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet-Diesel steady on sustained buying.

text.p: Singapore's physical gas oil market was steady to firmer on Friday amid sustained buying interests, after the swaps market rebounded strongly earlier in the day, traders said.

The swaps market for June gained as much as 50 cents per barrel, before eventually shaving off 15 cents from the day's high. June was traded at between $25.40 and $25.55 per barrel and July at $25.00.

Two physical cargoes were bought by a Japanese trader, one from a US major at $25.20 per barrel for May 31-June 4 lifting, free-on-board basis, up 10 cents from Thursday, and another at at $25.70 for June 11-15 lifting fob, from a European major. The second cargo was 35 cents more than Thursday's deal.
The Japanese trader have bought 900,000 barrels over two days. Traders said they expect sporadic purchases to continue into next week at current levels.

They said one of two gas oil cargoes purchased by Taiwan through a recent tender for June lifting was offered to China at $192 per tonne cost-and-freight basis. This was equivalent to $25.70 per barrel, c-and-f.
But traders said China would wait for prices to dip further before committing themselves.
Jet fuel was steady with offers seen at $24.75-$24.90 for end May-mid June liftings, with a deal heard done at parity to Singapore spot quotes for second-half June lifting, fob basis.
Traders said BB Energy was awarded Bangladesh's tender to buy 155,000 of kerosene for May 23-24 delivery at $1.09 per barrel above Singapore spot quotes c-and-f Chittagong.
